It said weakness in some currencies may be offset by strength in others because of its geographic diversity. It enters into forward exchange contracts and buys foreign currency options and collars (principally euro, British pound and Japanese yen) to hedge portions of forecasted cash flows denominated in foreign currencies. It also uses derivatives to further reduce its net currency exposure.

Coca-Cola estimated that a 10% weakening of the U.S. dollar would have decreased their fair value by $609 million.

For commodity risk, Coca-Cola said it manages its exposure primarily through supplier pricing agreements, which let it establish purchase prices for certain inputs used in manufacturing and distribution. When deemed appropriate, it also uses derivatives to further manage commodity exposure.

Coca-Cola said certain of these do not qualify for hedge accounting but are effective economic hedges that help mitigate price risk on purchases and transportation of materials used in manufacturing.
